text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German debt erased session gains in quiet, late afternoon trading, but dealers were not yet worried these losses would be extended, saying instead the market was still largely stuck in a range at higher levels. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.77, down 0.07 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended Tuesday's session in a spirited mood as traders report heavy buying at long end and switching into gilts from both core and peripheral European debt markets. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-09/32, up 18/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures looked set to remain rangebound on Wednesday as traders said they were reluctant to make big bets ahead of the outcome of a U.S. monetary policy council meeting. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.64 unchanged from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debts markets held higher in late afternoon in largely a technical correction after Monday's losses on EMU concerns, dealers say buying interest returned despite weakness of German bunds and T-bonds, slightly firmer lira against the mark helped give market support. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.79, up 0.55 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened moderately lower with the market range-bound just ahead of a two-day Federal Reserve monetary policy meeting, though the market expects the FOMC to leave monetary policy unchanged, trading is likely to have a cautious tone until the meeting ends on Wednesday. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-30/32, down 05/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.75 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly lower, speculation that investors' appetite for the newly auctioned four-year notes might be weaker than expected weighed down the March in the early afternoon. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.21, down 0.09 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw no dollar deals ahead of the U.S. FOMC meeting, but Brazil and Mexico together raised a total of 2.0 billion marks. Both deals were sold out amid huge demand for emerging market paper.
